paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Everybody in this room knew something. Pilate knew it was out of envy that Jesus was handed over to him (Matt 27:18). His wife called Him an "innocent man" (Matt 27:19). Pilate himself asked, "What evil has He done?" (Matt 27:23), and nobody could answer him.

So why did it still end the way it did? Because knowing the truth and standing on it are two different things. Pilate saw a riot starting, grabbed some water, and tried to wash it all off his hands. I'm telling you, friend, I've blamed a flat batch on the oven, the weather AND the flour, so I know that move. But water doesn't clean what's on your conscience.

And look at Jesus in the middle of all that noise. He gave no answer, not even to a single charge (Matt 27:14), and the whole time He stayed in the same spot. This story is not finished, friend, and we are not done being amazed. When the crowd gets loud, the truth doesn't get any smaller, so ask yourself where you'll stand.
